summariesJSON.title: Page 1
summariesJSON.content: This page provides detailed definitions and explanations of key cellular biology concepts. Cytology is introduced as the study of cells, establishing the foundation for understanding cellular processes. Cell Theory is defined as the principle stating all organisms consist of cells, an essential notion in modern biology. The page differentiates between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, highlighting prokaryotic cells as simple without nuclei, like bacteria, and eukaryotic cells as complex with nuclei, found in plants and animals. Key cellular structures include the plasma membrane (a selective barrier), nucleus (genetic control center), mitochondria (energy producers), and others like the chloroplast, ribosome, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosome, and vacuole each with specific roles. Definitions of crucial transport processes such as diffusion, osmosis, active transport, endocytosis, and exocytosis are provided. Also included are explanations of ATP’s role as an energy currency, photosynthesis and cellular respiration for energy conversion, and structural components like the cell wall, cytoplasm, chromosome, and phospholipid bilayer.
